programme.title: Britain's Most Fragile Treasure
programme.desc: Janina Ramirez explores the complex history of York Minster's Great East Window, the largest medieval stained-glass window in England. Composed of 311 panels, it was originally designed to tell the complete biblical history of the world from creation to the Last Judgement, and has been compared to Michelangelo's work at the Sistine Chapel. The historian closely examines the handiwork of its creator John Thornton, revealing intricate details that would not normally be visible, and follows a project to restore the window to its original glory

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: England v Ghana (Kick-off 9.00pm). Gabby Logan presents coverage of the Group L match at Boston Stadium in the USA, as both teams play their second game of the group stage. This is just the second time that these sides have ever met and the first time they've faced each other in a competitive fixture. The last time was back in March 2011, when former Sunderland striker Asamoah Gyan scored an injury-time equaliser to salvage a 1-1 draw at Wembley Stadium, cancelling out Andy Carroll's first-half finish, his first in international football. Ghana reached this tournament after finishing top of their qualifying group ahead of the likes of Madagascar, Mali and Chad. England also finished top of their group in the qualifying process, winning all eight games, scoring 22 times and not conceding once. The Three Lions will be hoping to make it through to the knockout stages for the third consecutive World Cup and have only been knocked out at the group stage once in their last seven appearances in the finals, since missing out on USA '94. England made an impressive start to their World Cup campaign on Wednesday as they beat Croatia 4-2, while Ghana also began positively with a 1-0 win over Panama. With analysis from Joe Hart, Wayne Rooney and Micah Richards

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Panama v Croatia (Kick-off 12.00am). Gabby Logan presents coverage of the Group L match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. This is the first-ever meeting between these two countries as they both go in search of three important points to boost their chances of making it through to the knockout stage. This is Panama's second appearance at the World Cup finals after they previously took part in the 2018 event, which was a tournament to forget for the CONCACAF nation as they finished bottom of their group with three defeats from three games, conceding 11 times in the process. In contrast, their opponents enjoyed their most successful World Cup eight years ago when they reached the final for the first time in their history, though that ended in defeat as they lost 4-2 to France in Moscow. Both these sides lost their opening group fixtures on Wednesday as Croatia were beaten 4-2 by England, while Panama conceded in second-half stoppage-time as they lost 1-0 to Ghana. With analysis from Ellen White

Brazil have been far from their imperious best so far in this tournament, but still have four points from two matches, while Scotland's win against Haiti may be enough to see them qualify, irrespective of the result here. There have been 10 previous meetings between these nations, four of which have been at the World Cup, and Scotland are still seeking a first-ever victory over the Seleção. The South Americans won three of those four World Cup clashes, the most recent of which was in the opening match of France '98 when an unlucky own-goal by Tom Boyd gave Brazil a 2-1 win, after a John Collins penalty drew Scotland level following a goal in the fifth minute by Cesar Sampaio. The last time they faced each other was a 2011 friendly at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, when a teenage Neymar scored both goals in a 2-0 victory, at a time when he had yet to make his reputation as one the leading players in world football, two years before he moved to Barcelona from Santos

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Czechia v Mexico (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the Group A match at Mexico City Stadium. The Mexicans were undefeated in the six matches they played here when hosting the 1970 and 1986 World Cups, and have continued in the same vein this time around, with a victory over South Africa here, before another win in Zapopan against South Korea ensured they were the first team to secure a place in the round of 32 and top spot in the group. In contrast, the Czechs have disappointed so far, collecting just one point against the South Africans, but a win would almost certainly send them through, either in second or as one of the best third-place teams

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Morocco v Haiti (Kick-off 11.00pm). Coverage of the Group C match at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Morocco have impressed so far, drawing with Brazil and beating Scotland, while Haiti have only pride to play for having already been eliminated. Not only is this the first-ever meeting between these nations, but it is also the first competitive game against a Caribbean team for Morocco, and a maiden competitive contest for Haiti against African opposition. By qualifying for this tournament, Haiti became the first Caribbean nation to qualify for a second time after first appearing in 1974, and while they are one of two nations from the region at this tournament, alongside Curaçao, there have only been five total Caribbean teams to compete at a World Cup, the last being Trinidad & Tobago in 2006. Morocco are one of nine African teams at this year's event, which is only the second time there have been more than five countries from the continent at any one tournament, with the previous record being six competitors at the 2010 World Cup, which was held in South Africa

The males begin to turn against each other, and one inexperienced lioness places her cubs in mortal danger as a rival group challenges the area's resident lions. programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026

programme.title: Ancient Autopsy

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: England v Ghana (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group L match at Boston Stadium in the USA, as both teams play their second game of the group stage. This is just the second time these sides have ever met and the first occasion they've faced each other in a competitive fixture. The last time was back in March 2011, when former Sunderland striker Asamoah Gyan scored an injury-time equaliser to salvage a 1-1 draw at Wembley Stadium, cancelling out Andy Carroll's first-half finish, his first in international football. Ghana reached this tournament after finishing top of their qualifying group ahead of the likes of Madagascar, Mali and Chad. England also finished top of their group in the qualifying process, winning all eight games, scoring 22 times and not conceding once. The Three Lions will be hoping to make it through to the knockout stages for the third consecutive World Cup and have only been knocked out at the group stage once in their last seven appearances in the finals, since missing out on USA '94. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Scotland v Brazil (Kick-off 11.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents coverage of the Group C match at Miami Stadium in the USA. Brazil have been far from their imperious best so far in this tournament, but still have four points from two matches, while Scotland's win against Haiti may be enough to see them qualify, irrespective of the result here. There have been 10 previous meetings between these nations, four of which have been at the World Cup, and Scotland are still seeking a first-ever victory over the Seleção. The South Americans won three of those four World Cup clashes, the most recent of which was in the opening match of France '98 when an unlucky own-goal by Tom Boyd gave Brazil a 2-1 win, after a John Collins penalty drew Scotland level following a goal in the fifth minute by Cesar Sampaio. The last time they faced each other was a 2011 friendly at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, when a teenage Neymar scored both goals in a 2-0 victory, at a time when he had yet to make his reputation as one the leading players in world football, two years before he moved to Barcelona from Santos

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Jordan v Algeria (Kick-off 4.00am). Coverage of the Group J match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in the USA, as the two teams meet for just the fourth time, and a first in 22 years. Jordan finished second in AFC third-round qualifying Group B behind South Korea to reach their first-ever World Cup. Four victories and four draws in 10 games were enough to earn 16 points and finish one point clear of Iraq to avoid going into the fourth round of qualifying and confirm their place at these finals. Algeria reached their fifth World Cup finals with more ease after finishing top of their qualifying group, ending up seven points clear of nearest competitors Uganda. They won eight of their 10 games, losing only once, to Guinea in a surprise 2-1 defeat all the way back in June 2024. Despite that setback in the third round of group fixtures, they went on to score 24 goals and concede just eight as they made it to the finals for the first time since 2014. At that event they finished second in their group behind Belgium on four points before losing 2-1 to Germany in the last 16. Both these sides lost their opening game of the tournament on Tuesday, with Jordan losing 3-1 to Austria and Algeria tasting defeat thanks to a 3-0 loss against Argentina

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Switzerland v Canada (Kick-off 8.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents coverage of both teams' concluding Group B match, held at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. The only previous meeting between these nations was a friendly match in 2002 that took place on Swiss soil, and saw the Canadians claim a 3-1 victory. This time around, both teams look all but certain to advance to the last 32 after each taking four points from their matches against Bosnia and Herzegovina and Qatar, with the co-hosts just needing a draw to guarantee top spot due to their superior goal difference. With analysis from Kevin Doyle

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Scotland v Brazil (Kick-off 11.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents coverage of the Group C match at Miami Stadium in the USA. Brazil have been far from their imperious best so far in this tournament, but still have four points from two matches, while Scotland's win against Haiti may be enough to see them qualify, irrespective of the result here. There have been 10 previous meetings between these nations, four of which have been at the World Cup, and Scotland are still seeking a first-ever victory over the Seleção. The South Americans won three of those four World Cup clashes, the most recent of which was in the opening match of France '98 when an unlucky own-goal by Tom Boyd gave Brazil a 2-1 win, after a John Collins penalty drew Scotland level following a goal in the fifth minute by Cesar Sampaio. The last time they faced each other was a 2011 friendly at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, when a teenage Neymar scored both goals in a 2-0 victory, at a time when he had yet to make his reputation as one the leading players in world football, two years before he moved to Barcelona from Santos

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Czechia v Mexico (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the Group A match at Mexico City Stadium. The Mexicans were undefeated in the six matches they played here when hosting the 1970 and 1986 World Cups, and have continued in the same vein this time around, with a victory over South Africa here, before another win in Zapopan against South Korea ensured they were the first team to secure a place in the round of 32 and top their group. In contrast, the Czechs have disappointed so far, collecting just one point against the South Africans, but a win would almost certainly send them through, either in second or as one of the best third-place teams

programme.desc: In the first of a two-part story, a fishing community is excited about the arrival of their festival queen for an annual celebration, but when her boat arrives with only her dead body on board, DI Mooney is left, yet again, with a baffling mystery to solve. What could a missing loaf of bread have to do with the crime? Meanwhile, Florence and Patrice look forward to their wedding, which is only a week away, but a huge strain is put on their relationship when the groom is drawn into the murder case as a former employer and long-time friend of the victim

programme.title: Saint-Pierre
programme.desc: Amidst several personal revelations, Arch's investigation into Gallagher comes to a head when a body washes up the shore

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: The Saint Marie Heritage Society is re-enacting the French invasion of the island when its president dies. At first it looks like an extreme reaction to a dodgy stew as the rest of the group have fallen ill - but when lab reports reveal there was poison in the pot, Humphrey is left wondering why the victim was the only one to end up in the mortuary. Meanwhile, Dwayne takes Humphrey out on the town to show him his own way of celebrating the founding of Saint Marie, and the DI continues to struggle with his feelings for Camille. Caribbean whodunit, guest starring David Bamber and Tyger Drew-Honey

programme.title: Father Brown
programme.desc: A visit to Chummy's holiday camp leads to another murder mystery for the sleuthing cleric. Mark Williams stars, with a guest appearance by Ted Robbins

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.sub-title: Beyond the Shining Sea - Part Two
programme.desc: Part two of two. The team are left stunned by another murder connected to the killing of festival queen Tiana. But there is a new lead - a phone call relating to their initial suspect - so DI Jack and his officers travel over to nearby Rosalie Island, where the owner and employees of a lucrative investment company all fall under suspicion as they are questioned about the mysterious call. Meanwhile, with emotions running high, Ruby encourages her uncle, Commissioner Patterson, to show his emotional side for once. Guest starring Angus Deayton and Saskia Reeves

programme.title: Hudson & Rex

programme.desc: The chef travels to the far west of Cornwall to meet a potter whose work captures the rugged beauty of her surroundings. Rick also whips up his favourite seabass dish

Rick also discovers a reason so many Germans love Cornwall
